raw_response:
I will keep my land simple this year. I have only 6 mu, so I will not scatter it too much. I will put 4 mu into the usual wheat-maize rotation and keep 2 mu for stevia. Wheat and maize are my steady crops. They feed the house and bring regular money. Stevia can bring cash, but it needs more watching, more hand work, and cleaner field management, so I will not expand it too much on a 6 mu farm.

For wheat, I will start from what has worked before in our area. I will use improved seed, put enough bottom fertilizer in, and with my well I will give three irrigations if the season is normal: one after sowing or at wintering if needed, one at jointing, and one at filling. I do not like saving too much on wheat fertilizer because once wheat is thin in spring, it is hard to pull yield back. For maize after wheat, I will go with hybrid seed and fast planting. If the stand is good, maize will pay back fertilizer better than cutting rates too hard. I will keep nitrogen a bit strong, and I will use no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time and moisture. For stevia, I will manage it more carefully than grain crops. I will keep the field clean, water more often, and not let it starve early. On my size of farm, I have to think about the whole pocket. Fertilizer, pesticide, and labor all pull from the same money. So I will spend solidly on the 4 mu wheat-maize land, and I will keep stevia at 2 mu where I can still handle it well with family labor.
